sources.matrix: own transitions (9.0, weighted by the HMM's regime probabilities) + the panel's HMM matrix (1070 companies, 12345 company-years) at K = 6

sources.growth: the HMM's regime means and spreads (2748/5044/4552 company-years per regime); spreads × 1.5, fitted in the walk-forward backtest so that the 80% range of revenue three years out holds about 80% of what happened (as estimated, the spreads made it too narrow)
sources.years_1_2: current fiscal year: 0.2% (7 analysts); next fiscal year: 2.4% (7 analysts)
sources.margin: trailing EBIT margin 4.6%; regime drift = panel median; κ = 0.16 (pooled regression, 9131 pairs)

backtest.text: Backtest (run in 2013–2019 on every filer's data as of then, 2,274 outcomes, without analysts' consensus): the 80% range of revenue three years out held 80% of what happened (11% fell below it, 9% above) — about right. That is with every regime's growth spread × 1.5, the one number fitted on these outcomes (and used here): as the hidden Markov model estimates them, the range held 68% (18% below, 14% above) — a single year's regime spread understates how far revenue can drift over several.
